messages:
Maya: Heads-up — SE escalated a customer: they get frequent 429s even though Console shows their daily quota as >80% available. Happening across several API keys. Repro steps below.

Maya: Repro (quick): 1) call /v1/generate with rate limit headers 2) observe 429s intermittently after ~100 reqs 3) Console > Usage > Quota heatmap shows zeros for that org for 5-10m windows.

Maya: Customer says enforcement is strict (their app is choked). They sent enforcer request IDs: r_8f7c2, r_8f7c3.

Aj: Interesting — did we see any ingestion lag on telemetry pipeline?

Keoni: Looking at metrics: there was a short window where the aggregation worker crashed and backfilled failed between 12:07–12:15 UTC. That lines up with the heatmap zeros. Possible delta-t alignment bug in the sampler.

Lina: @Keoni can you paste the enforcer logs for those request IDs? Need to confirm if enforcement saw a consumed count or a deny due to stale counts.

Keoni: Pasting trimmed enforcer log snippets:
```
2026-03-16T12:08:03Z enforcer[pid:42] req_id=r_8f7c2 org=acme allowed=false reason=quota_exceeded cache_state=miss counter=0 window_start=2026-03-16T12:00:00Z
2026-03-16T12:08:04Z enforcer[pid:42] req_id=r_8f7c3 org=acme allowed=false reason=quota_exceeded cache_state=miss counter=0 window_start=2026-03-16T12:00:00Z
```

Keoni: Notice counter=0 but allowed=false — that suggests enforcer consulted a stale or truncated counter.

Maya: Customer also captured `x-rate-limit-remaining` headers showing small numbers right before 429s, then zero after.

Aj: Hypothesis: sampler/aggregator had an off-by-one when computing window boundaries for our hourly/daily buckets. For some orgs we ended up assigning events to a different bucket and the realtime counter used by enforcer falls back to a different TTL and returns 0.

Lina: Can we check aggregator pod logs and the job that writes to the quota-store? Might be a timezone/epoch math bug.

Keoni: Found aggregator error: `panic: integer overflow when computing window_index` at 12:07:01 UTC. Backtrace shows function `compute_window_index(ts, window_size)` with window_size=3600 and ts truncated to seconds — we probably had a negative modulo somewhere.

Lina: Oof. That would explain zeros in UI and enforcer misses. If the aggregator wrote counters to the wrong key (off-by-one), enforcer's read path would not find the expected key and fallback path returns deny when caches are cold.

Oncall-SRE: Deploy bot just reported a rolling restart for aggregator-service at 12:10 for OOM; we should correlate.

deploy-bot: Deployed aggregator-service v1.14.2 -> v1.14.3 at 12:09 UTC (restart reason: OOM, hotfix applied).

Aj: Two parallel things then: (1) aggregator crash/backfill + (2) possible compute_window_index bug in v1.14.2. Hotfix may have reset state but customers still hit 429s while backfill catches up.

Maya: Customer wants ETA — they lost revenue. Can we give a timeline for visible fix in Console and stop additional 429s?

Keoni: Short-term mitigation: force-enforcer to use the fallback estimate path that allows burst until aggregator backfill completes. I can flip a flag in enforcer config to be permissive for orgs with missing counters. Risk = potential over-allow, but safer for customers.

Lina: I'll prepare a patch to compute_window_index with proper floor division and add unit tests. Pending PR, Keoni's config flip is reasonable.

Aj: Steps: 1) Keoni toggles permissive-enforcer flag for affected orgs (list from SE) 2) Lina merges fix and we roll aggregator patch 3) run backfill job to repopulate keys 4) monitor heatmap and enforcer denies.

Maya: SE provided list: acme-org, delta-inc, beta-studios. Keoni — can you toggle for those only?

Keoni: Toggled permissive-enforcer for acme-org & delta-inc at 12:23 UTC. beta-studios still pending confirmation of account id.

Keoni: Kicked off backfill job at 12:30 UTC (job id bf_20260316_001). Initial progress: 20% keys rewritten in 5m.

Maya: Customer confirmed reduced 429s for acme after toggle. :relieved: They still see some spikes when backfill lags.

Lina: PR opened: github.com/redwood/aggregator/pull/482 — fix compute_window_index + unit tests + add metrics for window-mismatch-count. Requesting review from Aj.

Aj: Reviewing now. Also adding a short-term dashboard alert for window-mismatch-count > 0.

Oncall-SRE: Monitor: backfill job had a retry flood at 12:39 due to redis timeouts, throttling the writes. Increasing concurrency from 4->8 helped.

Keoni: Backfill complete for acme-org & delta-inc at 12:58 UTC. Heatmap now shows correct counts. Enforcer denies stopped for acme.

Maya: Customer says negative business impact reduced, asking for RCA and postmortem.

Lina: I'll draft a short RCA and link to PR + logs + backfill job id. Action items: add unit tests, add extra monitoring, add graceful fallback in enforcer.

Maya: Thanks team — will update customer with timeline + RCA link when ready.

Aj: Follow-up: schedule a retro to review why OOM happened and why hotfix released without a canary.

Keoni: TL;DR root cause = aggregator OOM caused a crash/backfill + a compute_window_index off-by-one/integer issue in v1.14.2 which led to keys written to wrong window → console shows zeros and enforcer reads missing counters → denies (429). Mitigations = permissive toggle, backfill, patch, tests, monitoring.

Maya: Marking thread for postmortem and customer comms. /cc @Lina @Keoni @Aj

Maya: End.
